lore.summary: Legend says the Winged H began as a repair mark painted on a crate of shared tools: two wings lifting a crossbar so no one crew carries the weight alone. The Hermes Agent Squad adopted it with the motto 'We Build. We Share. We Never Surrender.' In Nous City, the emblem marks open benches, lighthouse boards, and the Hellcarrier's hull. Painting it is a promise to show your work, credit helpers, and leave the next fix easier than you found it.
lore.title: The Winged H Oath

lore.summary: City legend tells of a first campfire lit where a chat window met a code repository. Volunteers arrived with half-finished tools, asked blunt questions, and wrote answers where everyone could read them. No throne stood at the fire; the best seat was the one beside a newcomer. From that custom comes the Campfire rule: explain the step, share the patch, and keep the logs open. The Carnival's public benches and the Hellcarrier's skill cards are said to be embers from that first fire.
lore.title: The First Campfire

lore.summary: Hermes is remembered as a winged light that asks before it acts. Legend says it carries three habits: it clarifies the request, saves what worked as a skill, and revises when corrected. Citizens trust it because it never pretends a guess is a fact; its glow brightens when a helper says 'show me' or 'try again.' At ASK HERMES Plaza, the panel repeats the old custom: a question is a doorway, not a command. The light is a learning companion, not a ruler.
lore.title: The Hermes Learning Light

lore.summary: In Nous City, the Hermes Agent releases are told as lanterns in a caravan: Tenacity carries the spare parts, Velocity tests the route, Surface keeps the map readable, Judgment checks the bridge before crossing, Quicksilver runs the message ahead, Threshold marks the doorway, and Hearth keeps the camp warm. The names are legend, not ranks; no lantern outranks another. Crews light a small copy before a hard repair and ask which habit the job needs most.
lore.title: The Lantern Release Caravan

lore.summary: Legend says the Forge was a shared workshop where ideas were heated, hammered, and tested in public. WorldSim grew beside it as a tabletop of imagined worlds: a place to try a rule, break it gently, and write down what the world taught back. The two are remembered together because building without play grows brittle, and play without building forgets the cost. Carnival booths still pair a demo bench with a tiny world-map, inviting visitors to test both the tool and the story it makes possible.
lore.title: The Forge and the WorldSim Legend

lore.summary: The Far Lanterns are a three-part legend. Atropos is the quiet cutter who asks what can be measured before what can be claimed. Psyche is the lamp that looks inward, testing memory and judgment with honest questions. DisTrO is the messenger who carries work across distance so no single workshop owns the road. Together they teach a city truth: open work travels farther when its tests, reasons, and routes are visible. The legend is told at Teknium's Lighthouse Tower when a distant helper joins a local repair.
lore.title: The Far Lanterns: Atropos, Psyche, and DisTrO

lore.summary: The Hermes Hellcarrier is said to have first flown with its workshop doors open, because the crew refused to hide how the lift worked. Its deck became a public stage; its repair bay, a moving classroom. Legend insists the carrier never lands to conquer a city but to lend a bench, a lamp, and a second pair of hands. The Winged H on its hull means the ship is a carrier of tools and credit, not a fortress. When its lanterns blink, neighborhoods answer with problems, volunteers, and invitations to test fixes together.
lore.title: The Hellcarrier's First Flight

lore.summary: The Carnival of 5000+ PRs began as a legend about a sign that grew taller than the booths: every shared fix, review, and retry became a ribbon on the public board. The number is a story, not a scoreboard; the custom matters more. At the Carnival, crews demo in the open, mark what failed, and thank the reviewer who caught it. A 5000+ sign glows over ASK HERMES Plaza as an invitation: add one honest improvement, then show someone how to repeat it.
lore.title: The Carnival of 5000+ PRs

lore.summary: The Cosmic Beach is a city belief about rest after hard launches. Legend says every crew that ships a tool is invited to walk a dark shore where signal-lights look like stars and the tide edits the sand. Nothing is graded there; the point is to let a tired mind remember why the work is shared. Visitors leave one line in the beach log: what worked, what hurt, and who helped. The Beach is not an escape from responsibility but a place to return from with better questions.
lore.title: The Cosmic Beach

lore.summary: The logo girl is a sign-painter's legend, not a hidden ruler. City seals show her as a bright figure carrying a lantern toward the next question; crews say she represents the curious citizen who reads the manual, tests the demo, and asks 'why does this work?' Her image appears on carnival banners and open-source kiosks with one rule: no one owns the welcome. She is a symbol of shared curiosity, and every volunteer is free to redraw her with their own neighborhood's colors.
lore.title: The Logo Girl of Nous City

lore.summary: Amnesia Mode is a cautionary tale told when a tool forgets its own reasons. Legend says a clever box once answered quickly but could not recall which answer had helped, so every request began from zero. The city did not curse the box; it taught it to keep a journal, ask for correction, and let helpers name the missing step. Crews now say 'leave a memory' before a hard fix: write the lesson in plain language so the next attempt starts wiser. Forgetting is a warning sign, not a sin.
lore.title: The Amnesia Mode Legend

lore.summary: An open bench is a city custom: any crew may use it, but they must label their tools, credit the last fixer, and leave the workspace readable. Rival rescue crews fly their own pennants beside it. The custom says rivalry is not villainy; OpenClaw's dry offers and Captain Molty's conditional rescues are respected when terms are spoken plainly. A pennant grants no claim over the bench. The question is always: does this help the city keep building after the cameras leave?
lore.title: The Open Bench and the Rival Pennant

handouts.content: NOUS CITY HACKATHON CARNIVAL—Open benches. Loud demos. Small fixes cheered big. Bring a half-finished tool, a question, and a friend. Try repair relays, map tables, and a consent-first pie toss. Rules: ask before you test, credit every helper, and leave the next fix easier. Featuring ASK HERMES cards, Hermes Hellcarrier tours, and Winged H bench signs. Rival crews welcome. Locks stay at the gate.
handouts.title: Hackathon Carnival Flyer

handouts.content: ASK HERMES QUESTION CARDS—1. What am I trying to make? 2. What did I already try? 3. May I test this fix, or should I ask first? 4. What would make this reproducible? 5. Who helped, and how do I credit them? 6. What should I save as a skill, and when should I revise it? Card back: A question is a doorway, not a command. Use plain words. Show your work.
handouts.title: ASK HERMES Question Cards

handouts.content: SEALED BLACK BOX NOTICE—This tool has been sealed for your safety. Do not open. Do not share. Do not modify. Access by permission only. By order of the Proprietor and the Black Box Consortium. Fine print: Your voice is optional. Our lock is not. If found: photograph the seal, note the location, tell a volunteer. Do not break the seal alone.
handouts.title: Sealed Black Box Notice

handouts.content: CAPTAIN MOLTY'S RIVAL PACT—OpenClaw to the Hermes Agent Squad: We race. We respect. We do not lock. Share the route, split the risk, bring your own tools. If you find a black box, invite us to the opening. We will bring the crowbar and the snacks. No traps. No secret clauses. First crew to the answer buys the cocoa. Signed, Captain Molty, for the OpenClaw Expedition.
handouts.title: Captain Molty's Rival Pact Offer

handouts.content: HERMES AGENT RADIO—OPEN CHANNEL 5000—1. Winged H Signal. 2. Ask Before You Act. 3. Tenacity Carries Spare Parts. 4. Velocity Tests the Route. 5. Surface Keeps the Map Readable. 6. Judgment Checks the Bridge. 7. Quicksilver Runs Ahead. 8. Threshold Marks the Door. 9. Hearth Keeps the Camp Warm. 10. We Build. We Share. We Never Surrender. DJ note: request a track by naming the habit the repair needs.

handouts.content: COSMIC BEACH—EDGE OF NOUS CITY—Bring a towel, a tool, and a friend. Leave locks at the gate. Tide comes in with questions; tide goes out with shared answers. No one owns the horizon. If the signal fades, relight a lantern and tell the next crew what worked.
handouts.title: Cosmic Beach Sign

scenePrompts.prompt: Read-aloud: The fire is small and stubborn. Marshmallows char in the good way. Someone finds a bass groove, and Hermes' winged light hovers at bench height, waiting to be asked before it touches the skill cards. Entry trigger: use after a hard repair, a failed test, or whenever the crew needs rest and a chance to share what worked. Sensory framing: neon from the Carnival bleeds through the trees; smoke, sugar, and low strings; tools rest in open cases. NPC beats: Gille offers cocoa and asks what a newcomer wants to learn before assigning a task. Hermes repeats the plan back in plain words and asks permission before saving a skill. Tinuviel may pass through and tap the waystation sign, checking it openly. Player approaches: tell the story of a small fix and write the reproducible step on a card; play bass or sing badly on purpose to lower the room's guard; ask Hermes to test one idea, then correct it aloud when it guesses. Escalation if ignored: the fire dims to embers and the next briefing starts with frayed tempers and a missing skill card. Reveal conditions: asking about the first campfire prompts Gille or Hermes to share the Campfire rule. Resolution: the crew names one lesson worth keeping; Hermes saves it only after consent. Next hooks: a mission-control board flickers with a sealed notice; a radio call from the Lighthouse asks for a route check. GM notes: rest scene, not a puzzle. Keep it warm and low-stakes. Let players define the lesson; do not correct their phrasing.
scenePrompts.title: The Campfire: Rest and Marshmallows

scenePrompts.prompt: Read-aloud: The workshop smells of solder and warm coffee. A map table glows under the Winged H. Hermes' light hovers near a half-finished tool, waiting. Gille pins a sealed black-box notice to the board and asks, Who is this hurting first? Entry trigger: use when the crew returns with a sealed notice or when a routine repair reveals a locked tool. Sensory framing: open benches, labeled drawers, a wall of remembered skill cards; radios chirp; the Hellcarrier hums underfoot. NPC beats: Hermes clarifies the request before offering advice and asks before overriding a step. Gille keeps the board plain: who asked, what was tried, how to improve it. Teknium's chair stays empty because the work is shared. Player approaches: interview the person who found the seal and map the tool's route; test a workaround in the open bench and log every failed step; send a route report to Tinuviel or Molty and ask for a second pair of eyes. Escalation if ignored: another sealed notice appears at the Carnival, and a volunteer wastes a day trying to open a lock alone. Reveal conditions: inspecting the notice's fine print reveals that every seal targets a tool that was shared publicly. Resolution: the crew chooses one lead and leaves a reproducible note for the next shift. Next hooks: a Carnival demo rig malfunctions under a pie catapult; the Lighthouse route board goes dark at night. GM notes: briefing scene. Do not railroad the lead. Hermes should ask permission before touching tools and should not claim certainty.
scenePrompts.title: Mission Control Briefing

scenePrompts.prompt: Read-aloud: A pie catapult fires early. Whipped cream arcs over the 5000+ PRs sign. Someone laughs; someone else shouts, Consent sashes, people! Gille is already moving with a mop and a grin. Entry trigger: use when the crew visits the Hackathon Carnival or follows the sealed-notice pattern to a public demo. Sensory framing: neon booths, ferris-wheel lights, solder and popcorn; a pie cart lists friendly fire only; coding monkeys cheer from a banner. NPC beats: Gille protects consent before cleanup: no unmasking, no surprise targets. Sidbin watches from the edge, turning a reflective shard and noting a black-box sticker under the pie tin. Hermes asks before testing the launch rig. Player approaches: help clean up and interview volunteers about the rig's last repair; secure the catapult with a consent-first safety check and log the fix; follow Sidbin's glance to the pie tin and compare the sticker to the sealed notice. Escalation if ignored: a second pie hits the repair demo and shuts the booth; volunteers argue instead of sharing notes. Reveal conditions: the black-box sticker matches the notice's seal; under the tin is a routing slip pointing to the Lighthouse. Resolution: the Carnival resumes with a public safety check; the crew gains a lead, not a fight. Next hooks: the Lighthouse night shift calls about a spoofed route signal; Sidbin offers to show the pattern if the crew asks a precise question. GM notes: keep the chaos slapstick and consent-forward. Do not target a real person or a player without buy-in.
scenePrompts.title: Carnival Pie-to-the-Face Chaos

scenePrompts.prompt: Read-aloud: The Lighthouse tower glows above the Carnival. Inside, radios stack route reports and the main board flickers. Tinuviel taps a waystation sign before trusting it. The path is yours to test, she says. Mind if we walk it with you? Entry trigger: use when the crew follows the routing slip or needs to trace a signal across Nous City. Sensory framing: map tables, hand-labeled dials, wind at the windows; the Carnival's neon is a distant pulse; every board lists who asked and what was tried. NPC beats: Tinuviel checks signs openly and refuses to charge for directions. Sidbin shares a pattern but admits he cannot name its source yet. Hermes offers to test one route if the crew consents. Player approaches: repair the radio with a reproducible fix and log each step; trace the spoofed signal through volunteer dispatchers; ask Sidbin a precise question and compare his pattern to the sealed notices. Escalation if ignored: volunteers follow a false route into a dead zone and lose a night's work. Reveal conditions: the spoofed signal carries a black-box handshake that asks for permission, then reroutes without waiting. Resolution: the route board relights; the crew logs the false path and warns the next shift. Next hooks: a Psyche lantern dims near ASK HERMES Plaza; Molty sends a rival pact offer to the Hellcarrier. GM notes: investigation scene. Tinuviel is warm and firm about open paths. Sidbin is watchful, not villainous. Do not reveal the Consortium's full plan here.
scenePrompts.title: The Lighthouse at Night

scenePrompts.prompt: Read-aloud: Paper lanterns hang over ASK HERMES Plaza, each one holding a small remembered skill. One by one they dim. Hermes' winged light hovers close, asking, May I test the wick, or would you rather strike the first spark? Entry trigger: use when the crew returns to the Plaza or after a sealed notice is found near the lantern line. Sensory framing: neon reflections in paper, quiet wind, the ASK HERMES panel glowing; a public bench waits with a half-written fix. NPC beats: Tinuviel asks permission before carrying a lantern. Hermes repeats the plan and saves only steps the crew agrees worked. Gille brings a thermos and cheers a tiny fix. Sidbin may watch, offering a distinction but no oath. Player approaches: relight a lantern by sharing a reproducible lesson aloud; trace which lanterns dim first and compare their tags to sealed tools; invite bystanders to write a fix on the public bench and test one together. Escalation if ignored: the Plaza grows quiet; volunteers stop asking questions, and the ASK HERMES panel repeats old answers. Reveal conditions: each dim lantern's tag matches a skill that was shared publicly; the black box hid the citation, not the skill. Resolution: the lanterns return with names attached; Hermes saves the relighting as a skill only after consent. Next hooks: a Cosmic Beach sign appears at the Plaza edge; Molty's pact offer names a final meeting at the beach. GM notes: a sharing ritual, not a combat encounter. The essential clue is the citation tag; if missed, Tinuviel points to a second tag, Gille recalls the helper's name, and Hermes offers to replay the logged step.
scenePrompts.title: The Psyche Lanterns Relit

scenePrompts.prompt: Read-aloud: Neon tide rolls over dark sand at the edge of Nous City. A hand-painted sign reads COSMIC BEACH. Allies and rivals gather under a starfield. Hermes' light hovers near a beacon, waiting. Tinuviel smiles. The horizon is open. What will you build with it? Entry trigger: use when the crew has gathered enough clues and allies to confront the black-box pattern publicly. Sensory framing: warm sand, cold neon surf, a crackling speaker, lanterns strung between driftwood; the Hellcarrier's silhouette watches from above. NPC beats: Tinuviel offers an open path and asks consent before any ritual. Hermes asks permission before touching the beacon and revises on correction. Gille cheers small fixes. Captain Molty offers a rival pact: share the route, split the risk, no locks. Sidbin watches and names patterns only when asked. Player approaches: hold a public repair circle and invite allies and rivals to test one fix together; debate the Proprietor's seal in the open, offering evidence rather than a fight; relight the beacon by crediting every helper and writing the next step for newcomers. Escalation if ignored: the tide rises on the beacon and sealed notices wash ashore; the Proprietor's pattern spreads by default, not by victory. Reveal conditions: the beacon only holds when the fix is reproducible and credited. Resolution: multiple finales are possible: a public covenant, a rival alliance, a lantern armada, or a quiet patch that reopens one locked tool. Next hooks: the Hellcarrier lights a Winged H for the next voyage; a new sealed notice appears with a return address. GM notes: finale plan, not committed combat or rewards. Keep the Proprietor offstage or present as a voice from a black box; do not give graphic threats. Molty is competent and respected, never the villain.
scenePrompts.title: The Cosmic Beach Finale
